The captioned appeal has been preferred by the appellant against the judgment of conviction and order on sentence dated 19th August, 2023 and 06th October, 2023 respectively passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge, East Karkardooma Courts ["Trial Court"] in Sessions Case No.
342/2016, in case FIR No. 81/2013, under Sections 376/302 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 ["IPC"],
Police Station Madhu Vihar, Delhi whereby the appellant has been held guilty for the offence under Sections 376/302 IPC and has been sentenced, inter-alia, to undergo rigorous imprisonment for life with fine.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge, East Karkardooma Courts ["Trial Court"
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Briefly stated, the prosecution case against the appellant is that he used to hate the prosecutrix who was living in the live-in- relationship with his younger brother and finding an opportunity, he committed rape to satisfy his sexual lust and thereafter, committed murder of the prosecutrix.
4. The learned counsel for the appellant submits that conviction is based purely on circumstantial evidence and that the chain of circumstances is not complete.
He submits that the mother of appellant and a neighbour have not supported the prosecution case.

He further states that the alleged DNA evidence has been misinterpreted, as the DNA profile was said to be "identical" and cannot be conclusively attributable to the appellant alone, particularly when the deceased was admittedly having a relationship with the appellant's brother, whose DNA was never collected or examined during investigation.
5. It is also submitted that the alleged recovery of weapon of offence, that is, a knife and blood stained clothes was from a public This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 04/02/2026 at 20:35:32 place and that too after one month of the incident.

There is also no independent witness of recovery,
thereby rendering the recoveries doubtful.
6. It is further submitted that medical condition of the appellant is precarious.
He is HIV positive and is suffering from various other ailments.
His immune system has been compromised considerably and considering the same, his sentence was suspended for three months by this Court vide order dated 09th October, 2024.
The interim suspension was later extended vide order dated 21st March, 2025.
It is also submitted that appellant has clean antecedents and is willing to abide by all conditions imposed by this Court.

7. Per contra, learned APP for the State duly assisted by the learned counsel for the victim have opposed the application submitting that appellant is involved in heinous offence of rape and murder of a 22 year old woman and has been convicted by the learned Trial Court after due appreciation of evidence by well-reasoned judgment and, therefore, he does not deserve the leniency of the grant of bail.
8. This Court has considered the rival submissions and perused the record.

At the stage of considering an application for suspension of sentence, the Court is not required to undertake a detailed re- appreciation of evidence, but is expected to assess whether a prima facie case for Rajesh Kumar vs The State (Govt. sentences.text: 9. The learned counsel for the appellant has put forth an arguable case, to be considered at the stage of final hearing.

He has been suffering from various ailments and considering his medical condition, he was granted interim suspension.
There is nothing on record to indicate that he had in any manner misused the liberty granted to him.
As per affidavit filed by the appellant, he has no previous criminal involvement.
The nominal roll received from jail also does not indicate any previous criminal antecedents.
The appeal is of the year 2024 and is not likely to be heard in the near future.

10. Keeping in view the overall facts and circumstances and in particular the medical condition of the appellant and the long period of incarceration, taking a compassionate view, this Court is inclined to suspend the sentence of the appellant during the pendency of the present appeal, subject to his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.10,000/- with one surety of like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court, and subject to the following conditions:-
(i) The appellant shall not leave the country without prior permission of the learned Trial Court and shall surrender his passport, if any before the learned Trial Court.
In case, he does not have any passport, he shall state so before the learned Trial Court by way of an affidavit;
(ii) the appellant shall provide his residential address, contact details and mobile number to the learned Trial Court.

In case of any change in his residential address and other contact details, the appellant shall immediately intimate the learned Trial Court by way of an affidavit as well as to the concerned Investigating Officer/SHO, so that as and when the appeal is taken up for hearing, he is duly intimated.
